title: Universal 1/f Noise in the Power Spectra of Energy Time-series in Solvated DNA Dynamics
authors: Harsh Sahu, Deepika Sardana, Pramod Kumar, Ajay Kumar Chand, Sobhan Sen, Sanjay Puri
abstract: We investigate energy fluctuations of solvated DNA in three conformations: G-quadruplex, Hairpin, and Duplex. Our comprehensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations demonstrate that the time-series of interaction energies for DNA self, DNA-water and DNA-ion show 1/f noise with a universal decay exponent $β\simeq 0.90$. We show that DNA topology and structural rigidity modulate its dynamic coupling with the surrounding hydration shell and mobile counter-ions. This coupling critically shapes the 1/f noise profile: DNA self energies in flexible structures (G-quadruplex, Hairpin) display pronounced low-frequency modes absent in the rigid Duplex. These findings reveal how the interplay between DNA topology and environmental coupling governs different stochastic behavior in biologically relevant forms of DNA.
summary: This work uses molecular dynamics simulations to study energy fluctuations in solvated DNA across three topologies. The key finding is that the energy time-series exhibit universal 1/f noise, with the degree of low-frequency spectral power directly correlating with the structural flexibility of the DNA conformation. This highlights how topological constraints govern the stochastic dynamics of biomolecules in solution.
main_problem: The study investigates the universal nature of 1/f noise in the power spectra of energy time-series fluctuations within solvated DNA dynamics, and how DNA topology modulates its coupling with the surrounding environment.
main_result: All analyzed energy time-series exhibit universal 1/f noise with an exponent $\beta \simeq 0.90$, but flexible structures (G-quadruplex, Hairpin) show pronounced low-frequency modes compared to the rigid Duplex.
method: The research employs comprehensive atomistic Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations to calculate energy fluctuations ($\delta E$) and subsequently analyze their power spectral density ($S(f)$) via the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is solvated DNA modeled in three distinct conformations: G-quadruplex, Hairpin, and Duplex. The environment includes explicit water molecules and mobile counter-ions, simulated using established force fields.
key_observables: Energy fluctuations ($\delta E_{DNA\text{-}DNA}$, $\delta E_{DNA\text{-}water}$, $\delta E_{DNA\text{-}ion}$), Pearson correlation coefficients ($\rho_{ij}$), and the power spectral density $S_{ii}(f)$ exhibiting $1/f$ noise.
important_parameters: The universal decay exponent $\beta \simeq 0.90$, and the structural rigidity differences between the three DNA forms.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is in a stationary regime for power spectrum calculation, and that the observed noise characteristics reflect the underlying physical coupling mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures show typical time-series and probability distributions of energy fluctuations, contour plots of bivariate distributions, and log-log plots of power spectra $S_{ii}(f)$ confirming the power-law scaling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes energy correlations ($\rho_{ij}$) between DNA self, water, and ion energies, demonstrating strong anti-correlation between water and ion energies. It then analyzes the power spectra $S_{ii}(f)$ across the three DNA structures, contrasting the low-frequency behavior dictated by structural flexibility.
why_interesting: The finding of universal $1/f$ noise across different structural states, coupled with the explicit link between structural flexibility and the low-frequency spectral components, provides insights into non-equilibrium dynamics relevant to biological energy dissipation.
